ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An orphan is (1 mark)
   A. a person who looks after children
   B. a woman whose husband has died
   C. a brother or a sister
   D. a child whose parents have both died

2. Which article do we use before 'honest man'? (1 mark)
   A. the
   B. a
   C. some
   D. an

3. What should you do first when you get a form? (1 mark)
   A. Read the instructions
   B. Fold it
   C. Start writing at once
   D. Sign it

4. A sentence ends with (1 mark)
   A. a comma only
   B. a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
   C. a capital letter
   D. a colon

5. Complete: 'Mother bought enough flour ___ chapati.' (1 mark)
   A. by make
   B. making
   C. for make
   D. to make

6. Language patterns: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. There is enough water to drink.
   B. There is water enough to drink.
   C. There enough is water to drink.
   D. There is enough water for drink.

7. A visual is something we (1 mark)
   A. understand by looking at it
   B. taste
   C. hear only
   D. smell

8. Which visual would help you find a place you have never been to? (1 mark)
   A. A recipe
   B. A joke
   C. A map
   D. A poem

9. Complete: 'Give the book to ___.' (Ann and Eve) (1 mark)
   A. theirs
   B. they
   C. them
   D. their

10. Where does the sender's address go in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. After the name
   B. In the middle
   C. At the bottom left
   D. At the top right

11. Listening and diet: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I would likes to be a nurse.
   B. I would like to be a nurse.
   C. I would like to being a nurse.
   D. I would like be a nurse.

12. Which is a sentence starter for sharing a story? (1 mark)
   A. My favourite part was...
   B. Yours faithfully...
   C. To whom it may concern...
   D. Dear Sir...

13. What is the superlative form of 'big'? (1 mark)
   A. bigest
   B. biggest
   C. biger
   D. more big

14. A narrative is (1 mark)
   A. a form
   B. a story that tells what happened
   C. a map
   D. a list of names

15. Intonation is (1 mark)
   A. the length of a word
   B. the spelling of a word
   C. the rise and fall of the voice
   D. a kind of computer

16. Which word has the /ʤ/ sound at the beginning? (1 mark)
   A. yellow
   B. chair
   C. giraffe
   D. treasure

17. Which online reading habit is safe? (1 mark)
   A. Giving your address to a website
   B. Visiting any page a stranger suggests
   C. Reading only pages approved by a teacher or parent
   D. Clicking every advert

18. Which sentence is a run-on sentence that needs full stops? (1 mark)
   A. I bought fish.
   B. I went to the market.
   C. We went home.
   D. I went to the market I bought fish we went home.

19. What is the best way to practise a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. Say it slowly first, then faster
   B. Say it as fast as you can straight away
   C. Read it silently only
   D. Whisper it once

20. Which word begins with /w/? (1 mark)
   A. vet
   B. water
   C. van
   D. very

21. What is rhythm in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The title of the poem
   B. The beat in the words
   C. The number of pages
   D. The name of the poet

22. Which is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The goat ran like the wind.
   B. The goat ran quickly.
   C. The goat was fast.
   D. The goat is a runner.

23. In which word is 'gh' silent? (1 mark)
   A. night
   B. cough
   C. tough
   D. enough

24. Which is a sign of good speaking fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking clearly at a steady pace
   B. Whispering so nobody hears
   C. Speaking as fast as possible
   D. Stopping after every word

25. Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Mama may, I go to the shop?
   B. Mama, may I go to the shop?
   C. Mama, may I go to the shop.
   D. Mama may I go to the shop.

26. According to the text, when should we wash our hands? (1 mark)
   A. Only on Sundays
   B. Only when we see dirt
   C. After using the toilet
   D. Never with soap

27. Which sentence uses the sense of smell? (1 mark)
   A. The tap drips.
   B. The wall is white.
   C. The towel is rough.
   D. The soap gives off a fresh smell.

28. Which is a good way to start a diary entry sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Dear Sir ...
   B. Yours faithfully ...
   C. Today I ...
   D. Chapter One ...

29. How do newspapers and magazines usually differ? (1 mark)
   A. Newspapers have no words
   B. Magazines have no pictures
   C. They are the same
   D. Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures

30. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'glad'? (1 mark)
   A. hapie
   B. hapy
   C. happpy
   D. happy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give two safety rules for using the internet. (2 marks)

32. State the difference between a factual question and an inferential question. (2 marks)

33. Give one direct question and one indirect question about a story of a birthday party. (3 marks)

34. Write a short speech of four sentences about protecting a river. (4 marks)

35. Write three tall letters and three tail letters. (3 marks)

36. Arrange in order and write as a paragraph: (a) Finally, we went home. (b) We arrived at the farm at nine. (c) Then we fed the goats. (3 marks)

37. Write a short dialogue of four lines between two learners about sending an email. (4 marks)

38. Write one sentence using 'while' with the past progressive. (3 marks)

39. Write two words with the sound /aɪ/ and use one in a sentence. (2 marks)

40. Explain why gestures should match your words. (2 marks)

41. Write one sentence in the present progressive and one in the past progressive about a farm. (4 marks)

42. Give two reasons why we must fill in forms carefully. (2 marks)

43. Explain the difference in meaning between 'hopping' and 'hoping'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

44. Write directions to walk from the school to the market on the map in the lesson. (3 marks)

45. Replace each plain word with a better describing word: nice room, dirty clothes, good smell. Write the new phrases. (3 marks)

46. Fill in with a, an or the: 'Mama bought ___ cabbage and ___ egg. ___ egg was big.' (3 marks)

47. Write two similes to describe a tractor and a hot day. (2 marks)

48. Explain why it is important to put the stress on the right syllable. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — a child whose parents have both died
   An orphan has lost both parents.

2. D — an
   The h in honest is silent, so an is used.

3. A — Read the instructions
   Instructions tell you how to fill in the form.

4. B — a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
   These are the marks that end sentences.

5. D — to make
   Use to + verb.

6. A — There is enough water to drink.
   Enough comes before the noun.

7. A — understand by looking at it
   Pictures, signs, maps and videos are visuals.

8. C — A map
   A map shows where places are.

9. C — them
   Them is the object form of they.

10. D — At the top right
   Address and date are at the top right.

11. B — I would like to be a nurse.
   The pattern is would like to be + noun phrase.

12. A — My favourite part was...
   It helps you tell what you liked.

13. B — biggest
   The last letter doubles: big, bigger, biggest.

14. B — a story that tells what happened
   It tells events in order.

15. C — the rise and fall of the voice
   It is the tune of our voice.

16. C — giraffe
   In 'giraffe' the g says /ʤ/.

17. C — Reading only pages approved by a teacher or parent
   Approved pages keep you safe online.

18. D — I went to the market I bought fish we went home.
   Three ideas are run together without full stops.

19. A — Say it slowly first, then faster
   Start slowly to get the sounds right, then speed up.

20. B — water
   'Water' begins with /w/, said with rounded lips.

21. B — The beat in the words
   Rhythm is the pattern of beats.

22. A — The goat ran like the wind.
   A simile compares using like or as.

23. A — night
   In 'night' the gh is not pronounced.

24. A — Speaking clearly at a steady pace
   Fluent speech is clear and steady.

25. B — Mama, may I go to the shop?
   A comma after the person addressed, and a question mark at the end.

26. C — After using the toilet
   The text lists after using the toilet, before eating and more.

27. D — The soap gives off a fresh smell.
   'Fresh smell' refers to smell.

28. C — Today I ...
   Diary sentences often start with 'Today I ...'.

29. D — Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures
   Newspapers are published often and carry news.

30. D — happy
   Happy has a double p.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not share personal details; tell an adult if something worries you; use approved sites.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has an answer stated in the text. An inferential question needs you to use clues and think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Direct: What time did the guests arrive? Indirect: Why do you think the girl was excited?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each question and 1 mark for correct types.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two points such as not throwing rubbish in the river and planting trees on its bank, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each element.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tall: b, d, h (or f, k, l, t). Tail: g, p, y (or j, q).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each set, up to 3, with a mark for correctness.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: We arrived at the farm at nine. Then we fed the goats. Finally, we went home.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence in the correct place.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: How do we send an email? B: First click Compose. A: Now I type the address. B: Then write your message and press Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line with correct speaker format.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Mother was cooking while I was doing my homework.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for while, 1 for was/were, 1 for verb-ing forms used correctly.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: kite, night. I fly my kite on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct words and 1 mark for a correct sentence.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: If they do not match, the listener may be confused about what you mean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for confusion and 1 for a clear reason.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The farmer is digging the field. The cows were eating grass.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence: 1 for the correct form of be, 1 for the -ing verb.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The reader depends on the information, so a mistake may cause confusion or lost messages. Wrong information may delay help.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Hopping' means jumping, for example 'The rabbit is hopping.' 'Hoping' means wishing, for example 'I am hoping to win.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both sentences.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk east to the roundabout, go straight east across the foot bridge and you will reach the market.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for east, 1 mark for the roundabout and 1 mark for the foot bridge and market.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: bright, tidy room; muddy, crumpled clothes; fresh smell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: a, an, The
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct article.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The tractor roared like a lion. The day was as hot as a burning coal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable simile.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wrong stress can make a word hard to understand, and it can change the word from a noun to a verb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
